# What this project does

GEM's Global Oil and Gas Plant Tracker (GOGPT) and Beyond Fossil Fuels' gasDB both list gas power plants
in Europe. This project lines the two up plant by plant and shows where they disagree enough to matter.
It also remembers review decisions so that an item someone has dismissed doesn't come back on every run.

There are two scripts:

| Script | When to run | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `full-compare.R` | Any time | "Where do GEM and BFF disagree right now?" |
| `bff-update.R` | After a new BFF release | "What did BFF just change that GEM doesn't reflect yet?" |

Both write an Excel workbook to `outputs/`. You fill in decisions in that workbook, and the next run reads
them back in.

Examples below come from the 26 Oct 2026 runs. The main one is **Mellach** in Austria, which is
**BFF plant AT-11** and **GEM location L100000100047**.

# Input files

| Folder | File | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| `data/gem/` | `GOGPT-all-<date>.csv` | GEM units, one row per unit. Has a GEM unit ID (`G…`), a location ID (`L…`) and an "Other IDs" column that can hold BFF IDs. |
| `data/bff/` | `gasDB_units-<date>.csv` | BFF units, one row per unit. Unit ID `AT-11-3` means plant `AT-11`, unit 3. Keep older releases here; `bff-update.R` needs the previous one. |
| `data/bff-gem-source-exchange/` | `bff-to-gem-mapping-<date>.csv` | BFF's list of which GEM IDs each BFF unit corresponds to, plus comments (e.g. "GEM excluded: sub-threshold"). |
| | `bff-to-gem-notes-<date>.csv` | BFF's changelog: which fields BFF changed on a unit, when, and the source. |
| | `gasDB_gem_national_ids-<date>.csv` | BFF unit → GEM unit IDs and national IDs. **Not used yet** (see [Plans](#plans-for-improvement)). |
| `data/` | `decisions.csv` | Every review decision so far. Keep it in git. |

The scripts pick the newest file in each folder, using the `YYYY-MM-DD` date in the file name. If a file has
no date in its name, its modification time is used instead.

# How a comparison is built

```
 read & clean  →  link IDs  →  group into plants  →  summarise each plant
      →  compare GEM vs BFF  →  apply past decisions  →  write workbook
```

## Step 1: Read and clean (`R/read.R`)

Both files are converted to the same columns (capacity, status, technology, years, coordinates and so on)
so they can be compared. Along the way:

- **Status** is lower-cased and mapped to a common vocabulary. For example, GEM's
  `cancelled - inferred 4 y` becomes `cancelled`. Each status is then put in a **status group**.
  `pre-construction` and `announced` both become `planned`, so GEM `announced` and BFF `pre-construction`
  count as the same.
- **Technology** in GEM is mapped to BFF's codes: `combined cycle` → `CCGT`, `gas turbine` → `OCGT`,
  `steam turbine` → `ST`, and so on. `unknown` (GEM) and `not found` (BFF) become blank.
- **Country** names are aligned. For example, BFF's `Bosnia & Herzegovina` becomes `Bosnia and Herzegovina`.
- **Scope:** BFF units with main fuel `biofuel` are dropped. GEM is limited to the countries BFF covers.
- **Retirement year** uses the actual retirement year if there is one, otherwise the planned one.

## Step 2: Link the IDs (`R/link.R`, `build_links()`)

A link is a claim that a GEM location and a BFF plant are the same plant. Links come from both sides:

| Side | Where it comes from | Example |
|---|---|---|
| GEM | GEM's "Other IDs (location)" and "Other IDs (unit)" | `Beyond Fossil Fuels: AT-11-3` on a GEM unit at L100000100047 → link L100000100047 ↔ AT-11 |
| BFF | The mapping file's GEM location ID, GEM unit ID, and "GEM unit ID in BFF if different" | Row `AL-1-1` → `L100000408827` (Roskovec) → link L100000408827 ↔ AL-1 |

Unit IDs are always reduced to plant and location level (`AT-11-3` → `AT-11`, and a GEM unit → its location).
Each link is then labelled:

- **both**: GEM and BFF both have the link. This is the healthy case: 962 links on 26 Oct.
- **gem_only**: only GEM has the link, so BFF's mapping is missing it (19).
- **bff_only**: only BFF's mapping has the link, so GEM is missing the BFF ID (37).
- **stale**: the link points at an ID that doesn't exist in the other file, or at a plant that is out of
  scope, e.g. biofuel (160). Stale links are not used for matching. They go to **ID issues**.

## Step 3: Group into plants (`build_clusters()`)

Most plants match one to one: on 26 Oct, 945 of the 976 linked clusters were one BFF plant and one GEM
location. Unit splits differ much more often, which is why everything is compared at plant level. A few
sites are split differently at plant level too:

- **Several BFF plants : one GEM location** (13). BFF often splits a site by phase or owner, e.g. Irsching
  4/5/6, Keadby 1/2/3, Castejón TotalEnergies/Iberdrola. GEM has one location.
- **One BFF plant : several GEM locations** (4). GEM splits by block, e.g. Besós 3/4, Aceca 3/4.
- **Joined only by a one-sided link** (12). If only GEM or only BFF has a link, it is often a wrong link
  rather than a real split, e.g. Arklow DUB20 Echelon (IE-3) linked to Moneypoint.

So all the linked IDs are joined into **plant clusters**: anything connected by a link, directly or
through another ID, is one cluster.

> Example: if BFF plant `DE-10` links to GEM `L1` and `L2`, and `L2` also links to `DE-11`, then
> {DE-10, DE-11, L1, L2} is one cluster.

Each cluster gets a key made of its sorted BFF IDs and GEM IDs: `AT-11 | L100000100047` for Mellach. This key
is how decisions are remembered between runs. Plants with no link become one-sided clusters, e.g. `AT-3 | `.

## Step 4: Summarise each plant (`R/summarise.R`)

Each side's units are added up into one row per cluster:

| Field | How it is calculated |
|---|---|
| capacity | Sum of unit MW, **excluding cancelled** units |
| status | MW by status group, e.g. `operating 838 \| mothballed 165` |
| technology | MW by technology, excluding cancelled units |
| start_year | Earliest–latest start year, excluding cancelled and retired units |
| retire_year | Earliest–latest retirement year, excluding cancelled units |
| location | Average of the units' distinct coordinates |

Mellach comes out as:

| | GEM | BFF |
|---|---|---|
| capacity | 1084 | 1003 |
| status | operating 1084 | operating 838 \| mothballed 165 |
| technology | CCGT 838 \| ST 246 | CCGT 838 \| ST 165 |
| start_year | 2012–2020 | 1986–2012 |

## Step 5: Compare (`R/compare.R`)

Only clusters with both a GEM side and a BFF side are compared. Each field has its own rule, and all the
thresholds are in `config.R`.

**Capacity:** flagged if the gap is **more than 20 MW and more than 10%** of the larger value
(`cap_rule = "and"`).

> Mellach: 1084 vs 1003 → gap 81 MW, 7.5%. More than 20 MW but **not** more than 10%, so it is **not flagged**.

**Status and technology:** these compare the *mix*, not the total. BFF's profile is first scaled to GEM's
total, so a plant that is simply bigger on one side isn't flagged again here. Then each category is tested
with the capacity rule.

```{r mix-example}
gem <- c(CCGT = 838, ST = 246)
bff <- c(CCGT = 838, ST = 165)
bff_scaled <- bff * sum(gem) / sum(bff)   # rescale BFF to GEM's 1084 MW
round(bff_scaled)
gap <- abs(gem - bff_scaled)
round(gap)                                 # ST differs by ~68 MW...
round(gap / pmax(gem, bff_scaled), 2)      # ...which is 28%  -> technology flagged
```

> Mellach status: BFF has 165 MW `mothballed` and GEM has none, so status is flagged too.

**Start and retirement years:** flagged when either end of the range differs by **more than 1 year**.

> Mellach: 2012–2020 vs 1986–2012 → flagged.

If only one side has a year, `one_sided_years = "gem_missing"` means it is flagged only when **BFF has a year
and GEM doesn't**.

**Location:** flagged when the two plant centres are **more than 2 km** apart.

So Mellach appears on **Divergences** with `flags = status, technology, start_year`, and those cells are
highlighted. On 26 Oct there were 418 plants on that tab.

## Step 6: Plants with no match

Clusters that exist on only one side go to **BFF-only plants** or **GEM-only plants**. Two things are added
to each:

1. **BFF's mapping comment.** If it matches `explained_comment_regex` (e.g. "sub-threshold", "before 2023",
   "excluded: retired"), the plant is considered explained. It moves to **Explained absences**, which is
   for information only.
   Other comments, like "We found different information", stay visible next to the plant.
2. **A suggested match** (`suggest_links()`). It looks for a plant in the same country on the other side.
   Names are cleaned first: lower-cased, accents removed, and words like "power station", "CHP" and "gas"
   dropped. Then:
   - Within 5 km, it picks the most similar name. That is **strong** if similarity ≥ 0.6, otherwise
     **nearby, different name**.
   - If nothing is within 5 km, it offers a name with similarity ≥ 0.9 anywhere in the country
     (**similar name, far or no coordinates**).

> Example: BFF **Trebovice** (CZ-21) → suggested GEM **Trebovice power station**, 0 km → *strong*.
> If that's right, the fix is to add `CZ-21` to GEM's Other IDs. Next run it becomes a matched plant.

## Step 7: ID issues

All the problems with the IDs themselves are collected on one tab:

| Issue | What to do |
|---|---|
| GEM is missing this BFF ID (link only in BFF mapping) | Add the BFF ID to GEM |
| BFF mapping is missing this link (link only in GEM) | Tell BFF, or check GEM's link is right |
| BFF links a GEM ID that is not in the GEM file | The GEM ID was probably merged or deleted; tell BFF the current one |
| GEM links a BFF plant ID that is not in the BFF file | BFF removed or renumbered the plant; fix GEM's Other IDs |
| … outside scope (excluded fuel) | Usually fine. The plant is biofuel in BFF |
| Several BFF plants share one GEM location (check BFF split is intentional) | Usually fine. Once checked, mark `agree_to_differ` / `permanent` |
| One BFF plant covers several GEM locations (check GEM split is intentional) | Check GEM hasn't duplicated the plant; if not, `agree_to_differ` / `permanent` |
| Plant cluster held together by a link only one side has (check the link) | Often a wrong link. `detail` lists the one-sided link(s); remove the wrong one on whichever side has it |
| Several BFF plants and GEM locations in one cluster (check the links) | Check each link; usually two plants on the same site |

For cluster issues, `detail` gives the shape, e.g. `2 BFF : 1 GEM`. The item key lists every ID in the
cluster, so a decision holds until an ID joins or leaves the cluster, and then the issue comes back. A
one-sided link in a "held together" cluster also appears on its own as a "missing this link" row. Fixing the
link clears both.

## Step 8: Decisions (`R/decisions.R`)

Every review tab has `decision`, `scope`, `apply_to` and `notes` columns.

| decision | Meaning | Hidden next time? |
|---|---|---|
| `agree_to_differ` | A real difference we're keeping | Yes |
| `gem_updated` | GEM has been changed to match | Yes |
| `bff_likely_wrong` | Worth telling BFF | Yes |
| `investigate` | Still open | No, shown as "investigating" |

| scope | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `until_changed` (default) | Hidden while both values stay within the thresholds of what you reviewed |
| `permanent` | Never flag this field for this plant again |

Each workbook records the values it showed in a hidden `_values` sheet. That's what makes `until_changed`
work:

> You mark Mellach's `technology` as `agree_to_differ` while GEM is `CCGT 838 | ST 246` and BFF is
> `CCGT 838 | ST 165`.
>
> - GEM later changes ST to 250 MW: still within the thresholds, so it **stays hidden**.
> - BFF later changes ST to 0: a real change, so it **comes back** as "values changed since review",
>   with your old note shown.

`apply_to` limits a decision to some of a row's flags. For example, `status` decides only status for
Mellach and leaves technology and start_year open.

On each run, decisions are read from **every** workbook in `outputs/` into `data/decisions.csv`. If one
workbook is edited, its decisions replace the earlier ones from that workbook. For each item, the most
recent decision wins. Hidden items are listed on the **Reviewed** tab, where they can be re-decided.

# Outputs

## `full-compare.R` → `outputs/full-compare-<timestamp>.xlsx`

| Tab | Contents | 26 Oct |
|---|---|---|
| Summary | Files used, rows per tab, flags by country, link coverage, settings | |
| Divergences | Matched plants with at least one flagged field, side by side, plus BFF's latest note and sources | 418 |
| BFF-only plants | BFF plants with no GEM link, plus suggested match and BFF comment | 40 |
| GEM-only plants | GEM locations with no BFF link, plus suggested match and BFF comment | 169 |
| ID issues | See Step 7 | 247 |
| Explained absences | Unmatched plants BFF's comments already explain | 68 |
| Reviewed | Items hidden by decisions | |

## `bff-update.R` → `outputs/bff-update-<timestamp>.xlsx`

This script compares the **newest** BFF release with the **previous** one, then keeps only the changes GEM
doesn't reflect yet.

1. **What BFF changed.** The cutoff is the latest `Last update` in the previous release (27 Apr 2026). Units
   updated after the cutoff count as **changed**. IDs only in the new release are **new**, and IDs only in
   the old release are **removed**. For changed units, the key fields are compared release to release to
   say what changed.
   On 26 Oct: 361 changed, 38 new, 45 removed.
2. **Does it matter to GEM?** The full comparison is run twice, against the new release and against the
   previous one. A divergence is kept only if:
   - it is in a field BFF changed (a status change can affect status and capacity), **and**
   - it is new in this release, or BFF's value is different from last time.

   So older disagreements that BFF didn't touch don't fill this workbook.

> Mellach: BFF changed unit AT-11-3 `status: operating -> mothballed; technology: OCGT -> ST;
> start_year: 2020 -> 1986`. GEM still differs on all three, so it is listed with that change text in
> `bff_fields_changed`.

| Tab | Contents | 26 Oct |
|---|---|---|
| Divergences | Plants where BFF's change created or moved a divergence | 71 |
| New BFF plants | New BFF plants that aren't linked to GEM and aren't explained | 16 |
| Removed BFF units | Units BFF dropped that GEM still has as active (not retired or cancelled) | 17 |

Decisions made in either workbook apply to both scripts.

# Settings (`config.R`)

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `cap_pct`, `cap_abs_mw`, `cap_rule` | 10%, 20 MW, "and" | When a capacity (or status/technology) gap counts |
| `max_dist_km` | 2 | Location flag distance |
| `year_tol` | 1 | Year difference allowed |
| `one_sided_years` | "gem_missing" | What to do when only one side has a year |
| `exclude_bff_fuels` | biofuel | BFF fuels left out |
| `suggest_link_km`, `suggest_name_sim` | 5 km, 0.6 | Match suggestion search radius and "strong" name similarity |
| `explained_comment_regex` | see file | Which BFF comments count as explained |
| `gem_status_map`, `status_groups`, `gem_tech_map`, `country_map` | see file | Vocabulary alignment |

# Plans for improvement

## Planned

1. **Use BFF's GEM-ID file (`gasDB_gem_national_ids`).** Join it to the latest BFF units so each BFF unit
   has the GEM unit IDs BFF itself assigns. Compared with the 26 Oct files:
   - It covers 2,005 of 2,037 units.
   - 1,866 units have the same GEM IDs as the mapping file and 101 differ.
   - 38 of its GEM IDs aren't in GEM's file.
2. **Restrict file picking.** In `data/bff/`, read only `gasDB_units-*.csv`, so a stray file can't be taken
   for the latest release.
3. **Unit-level matching in both directions.** Compare each GEM unit's BFF ID with each BFF unit's GEM ID and
   label every pair **agree / one-sided / conflict / stale**. Build plant clusters from agreeing and
   one-sided links. Send conflicts to review instead of merging plants. Flag divergences only after this
   step.
4. **ID reconciliation tab.** One row per fix, saying who needs to act. For example:
   - "GEM unit G… should add BFF ID AT-11-3"
   - "BFF lists G…, which no longer exists"
   - "Mapping file and BFF release disagree for unit X"

   The aim is to raise the share of links that **both** sides agree on.
5. **Unit-level match suggestions.** For unlinked units inside an already-matched plant, suggest the
   matching unit from unit name, capacity and distance, so the strong ones can be accepted in bulk.
6. **"BFF suggestions" tab.** At the moment BFF's notes, with their sources, only appear when a plant is
   already flagged. Instead, list every note, and every mapping comment that asks GEM for a correction, with
   a status:
   - **GEM already reflects this**: the values now match, or GEM was updated after the note.
   - **Still differs**: shown with BFF's source.

   Same decision columns as the other tabs.

## Ideas to look into

- **National IDs as a third key.** Check whether GEM stores national IDs in "Other IDs". If it does, use
  them to confirm or suggest links.
- **Missing vs different.** A blank on one side is currently counted as a difference. For example, Vlora
  (AL-2) is flagged for technology only because GEM's is `unknown`. These could be a separate "missing data"
  flag so they don't mix with real disagreements.
- **Move `R/` into a package** with tests for the comparison rules, as the code layout already allows.
